why: SQLite 3.22.0 built as an ordinary program keeps an 8-byte size header in front of every block unless it can ask the heap for a block's size (HAVE_MALLOC_USABLE_SIZE, which configure defines on Linux). With the header, the shell's first mutex faulted: capstone-exec: domain fault cause=6 in pthread_mutex_init, a 16-byte store to an address 8 bytes off its boundary in the level0 arena (-O2 and -O0 alike). musl's own malloc_usable_size (oldmalloc) reads a chunk header level0 does not keep.

images.control: the same contract source with level0.c as on musl-fcntl-lock-pointer: malloc_usable_size resolves to musl's src/malloc/oldmalloc/malloc_usable_size.o

usable_size_mode: malloc_usable_size(NULL) == 0; for sizes 1, 4, 13, 40, 121, 364, 1093, 3280: two blocks, the reported size of the first at least the request, the whole reported range written, the neighbour allocated after it unchanged, a pointer stored in the last aligned slot reported read back
control: usable-size: status 255, capstone-exec: domain fault cause=7 (a store access fault while writing the size oldmalloc reported)
libc_test: not rerun: the change adds a function, and no libc-test source calls malloc_usable_size
not_covered: the Sublet heap (sublet_heap.c) has no malloc_usable_size yet; a program built with --heap sublet that calls it links musl's oldmalloc version
